drivingQuestion: When Beit Hillel validated slaughter with a harvest sickle, did they permit the meat for consumption or only free the carcass from the impurity of a neveila?
outcomeNote: R' Yoḥanan's limitation of Beit Hillel is left standing, but Rav Ashi's attempt to prove it from the mishna's wording is refuted: פוסלין/מכשירין and אוסרין/מתירין are one idiom.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַף כְּשֶׁהִכְשִׁירוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל, לֹא הִכְשִׁירוּ אֶלָּא לְטַהֲרָהּ מִידֵי נְבֵילָה, אֲבָל בַּאֲכִילָה אֲסוּרָה. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי ״בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין״, וְלָא קָתָנֵי ״בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹסְרִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין״. וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, לִיתְנֵי ״בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַמְּאִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין״! אֶלָּא, פּוֹסְלִין וּמַכְשִׁירִין וְאוֹסְרִין וּמַתִּירִין – חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Even when Beit Hillel deemed» the slaughter «valid, they deemed» it «valid only to purify it from» the ritual impurity of «an unslaughtered carcass; but its consumption is prohibited. Rav Ashi said:» The language of the mishna «is also precise, as» the tanna «teaches: Beit Shammai deem» the slaughter «not valid and Beit Hillel deem» it «valid, and he does not teach: Beit Shammai prohibit and Beit Hillel permit» its consumption. The Gemara objects: «But according to your reasoning, let» the tanna «teach: Beit Shammai deem» the carcass «ritually impure and Beit Hillel deem» it «ritually pure. Rather,» the terms «deem» it «not valid and deem» it «valid and» the terms «prohibit and permit are» all «one matter,» and no inferences may be drawn from that phrasing.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan limits Beit Hillel's validation in the preceding mishna to freedom from carcass impurity
moves.about: that Beit Hillel validated the sickle-slaughter only to spare the carcass the impurity of a neveila

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אשי: דיקא נמי, דקתני
moves.summary: the mishna's choice of 'invalidate/validate' supports the limitation
moves.about: quotes the mishna's own wording — פוסלין/מכשירין rather than אוסרין/מתירין

moves.summary: on that reasoning the mishna should have spoken of purity and impurity
moves.about: on Rav Ashi's own logic the mishna should have said 'Beit Shammai deem impure and Beit Hillel deem pure', since he takes the dispute to concern impurity alone

moves.summary: the linguistic proof collapses: the two idioms mean the same thing
moves.about: whether anything can be inferred from the mishna's choice of words — 'invalidate/validate' and 'prohibit/permit' are one and the same idiom

edges.proposedPredicate: interpret.limits_dispute_scope — «לא הכשירו אלא» — restricts how far a party's ruling in a dispute was meant to extend, without reinterpreting its words
